name: Xanthinuria Type II

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Xanthinuria Type II

criteria.description: Persistently low serum uric acid levels
Elevated urinary xanthine and hypoxanthine excretion
Deficiency of molybdenum cofactor sulfurase enzyme activity
Identification of pathogenic mutations in MOCOS gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low serum uric acid, increased urinary xanthine excretion, and demonstration of molybdenum cofactor sulfurase deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if biochemical criteria are met

pathognomonic.notes: Formation of xanthine kidney stones due to insoluble xanthine accumulation
Markedly decreased serum uric acid levels

common.notes: Repeated kidney stone episodes causing flank pain and hematuria
Acute pain due to obstruction by xanthine stones
Mild protein leakage in urine secondary to renal damage
Generalized fatigue due to compromised kidney function

occasional.notes: Microscopic or gross blood in urine
Mild to moderate decline in kidney function
Non-specific abdominal pain related to urolithiasis

rare.notes: Rarely mild cognitive or motor deficits reported
Joint pain possibly related to crystal deposition

laboratory: Elevated urinary xanthine and hypoxanthine levels
Normal or decreased serum molybdenum cofactor sulfurase activity
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing hyperechoic kidney stones
CT scan confirming radiolucent xanthine calculi
other: Negative response to allopurinol therapy (distinguishing from xanthinuria type I)

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple enzyme deficiencies including sulfite oxidase

redFlags: Severe hypouricemia with elevated urinary xanthine
Progressive renal impairment despite standard treatments
references: Ichida K, Amaya Y, Kamatani N, et al. Clinical and molecular analysis of xanthinuria type II. J Clin Invest. 1997;99(9):2391-2398.
Garrod AE. The incidence of alkaptonuria: a study in chemical individuality. Lancet. 1908;1(2521):1616-1620.
